description: Maps this grammar's ANTLR rule names onto flix-spec's canonical TreeKind vocabulary. Written by starting empty and working down the report's frequency-ranked `unmapped` list, which is the workflow flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md prescribes: map what is genuinely the same node, declare our own wrappers transparent, and leave the rest unmapped rather than guessing -- a wrong mapping reports as agreement and is worse than a gap.

notes.declaration: A wrapper around every declaration together with its doc, annotations and modifiers, where the reference makes those direct children of Decl.Def. Transparent at arity <= 1 and spliced by `declPrefix` otherwise.
notes.definitionName: A wrapper around the name rule, where the reference's Ident holds its token directly. Mapping both onto Ident gave Ident-inside-Ident and an arity divergence on every declaration -- 126 of them, the single largest class in the first measurement.
notes.expr: Left unmapped deliberately. It is a precedence level, transparent at arity <= 1 via `ignored`; mapping the branching case to Expr.Binary raises depth 88% -> 94% and drops agreement 76 -> 40, which is the signature of a guess that is often wrong. flix-spec's guidance is explicit: leave it unmapped rather than guess, because a wrong mapping reports as agreement and is worse than a gap. What it needs is the positional analysis tree-sitter-flix did, not a name-level rule.
notes.modifier: The reference groups modifiers in ModifierList and holds each as a token, with no per-modifier node, so ours is transparent rather than mapped.
notes.nameLowercase: The reference has one Ident kind and distinguishes case lexically rather than structurally, so all four name rules map onto it.
notes.primaryExpr: A precedence level, transparent on every expression that does not use its operator -- the same shape flix-jetbrains-plugin's ADDITIVE_EXPR has.
notes.usesOrImports: The reference emits UsesOrImports.UseOrImportList on every file, empty or not; ANTLR omits an optional rule that matched nothing. Declared transparent on both sides, because handling only one side is worse than handling neither -- the other side's wrapper then faces a real node and reports a modelling difference as a disagreement.
